subject: Film & Cinema
title: Surrealism: The Unconscious on Film
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Surrealism: The Unconscious on Film.

hook.text: In 1929, Buñuel and Dalí sliced an eyeball on screen. Cinema would never be the same.

buildup.text: Surrealist filmmakers drew from Freud, using cinema to visualize the unconscious mind.

discovery.text: Un Chien Andalou had no plot — just a stream of shocking, dreamlike images.

twist.text: Surrealism rejected logic. If an image felt emotionally true, that was enough.

climax.text: David Lynch, Alejandro Jodorowsky, and music video art all descend from this tradition.

punchline.text: The weirdest films feel the most honest.

quiz.question: What was the surrealist approach to filmmaking?
options: Visualizing the unconscious mind through dreamlike imagery
